headline: PLTR reports Q2 after tonight's close, with consensus at $1.81B and 81% growth, down from a record 85% last quarter.
quick: The weekend undid last week's driver. Trump called off a planned strike on Iran on Sunday and said talks resume today. Brent fell as much as 7.3% to $81.55. Index futures rose.
The relief is not spread evenly. Premarket, software is up and silicon is down: MSFT +1.8%, GOOGL +1.8%, META +1.2%, against MRVL -1.6%, INTC -1.6%, NBIS -1.3%, NVDA -0.4%.

Everything below the macro section is premarket and provisional. Volume before the bell is thin and these moves reverse often. The open settles it. PLTR reports after tonight's close, the only hard company event on the list.

macro.dt: Iran, and the oil unwind. Trump said on Sunday he called off a "massive attack" after Gulf allies pressed for a deal, and that talks restart today. Brent for October fell as much as 7.3% to $81.55; WTI traded near $80 against Friday's $84.67 settle. Reports differ on the exact drop, between 5% and 7.5%, because they quote different contracts
macro.dd: Oil was the whole chain last week: crude up, headline inflation up, rate-rise odds up, and a higher rate used to value distant profits. Take 7% off crude and the chain runs backwards. Tech holds most of its earnings far in the future, so it gains the most per point of yield relief.

macro.dt: The bond market barely moved. The 10-year yield fell just over 1 basis point to 4.688%. The 30-year fell about 4 basis points to 5.226%, still near Friday's 19-year high of 5.25%. Iran's foreign ministry then said on Monday it has no immediate plan for direct talks with Washington
macro.lead: This is the day's real tell
macro.dd: A 7% oil collapse bought four basis points at the long end. That says last week's yield damage was never mainly about oil. It is about government borrowing and doubt over the Fed's next move. So the funding-cost headwind on capital-hungry names does not lift with the oil price, which is exactly what the premarket split shows.

macro.dt: QQQ indicates near 691 premarket, about +0.47% on Friday's 687.99 close. Nasdaq-100 futures were up about 0.59%. The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,489.72
macro.dd: Half a percent is a thin reward for unwinding a month-long war premium in crude. Either the market doubts the truce holds, and Tehran's Monday comment supports that, or it never priced the war as heavily as the oil tape implied. Treat the number as provisional until the bell.

entries.happened: Palantir reports second-quarter results after tonight's close, the only confirmed company event on the list.
figures: Last quarter: revenue $1.6B, +85% y/y, the company's highest growth rate ever
Company's own full-year guide, raised in May: $7.656B, +71%, with US commercial up at least 120%
Options price a move of roughly 12% either way; the stock closed Friday at $123.06, well below its high
entries.why: Palantir is priced on the growth rate, not this quarter's profit. Consensus already assumes it slips from 85% to 81%, so meeting it confirms the peak is behind. What decides the stock is the full-year guide. Each raise extends how many years investors assume this compounding lasts, and that assumption, not the quarter, is most of the share price.

foot.v: Cannot be. The premarket +3.4% is positioning ahead of the print, not a reaction to it. Nothing has been reported. Eight straight beats mean a beat alone is the base case, so the bar is a raise.
US commercial growth falls below the 120% full-year guide, since that line is the entire agentic-AI case for the stock.
Tonight, after the close.

entries.happened: Microsoft indicates near $473 with nothing company-specific in the window.
figures: Last news: Wednesday's quarter, five sessions ago
entries.why: This is the oil unwind reaching the names that fund growth from their own cash. Microsoft's Azure case rests on demand it has already contracted, so a lower discount rate lifts it without needing cheaper debt. That is why it leads a risk-on tape while the borrowers lag.

foot.v: Premarket only, so provisional. There is no company news to price. This is the sector and the macro, not Microsoft.
The Iran talks collapse today and crude retakes $88, putting the discount-rate pressure straight back on.
Q1 FY27 results, late October.

entries.happened: Alphabet indicates near $362 on no company news, extending Friday's 6.7% gain.
figures: Its quarter was 22 July, twelve days ago
entries.why: Two straight sessions of gains on no news means the buying is positional, not informational. Investors are moving money into the cash-rich end of large-cap tech while the funding cost for everyone else stays high. That widens the valuation gap between self-funded and debt-funded AI.

foot.v: Nothing to price. Flag this one: a second large move without an event usually means flows, and flows reverse faster than facts.
The $195–205B capex guide comes back into focus as long yields resume rising, since that spend is what the market punished in July.
Q3 results, late October.

entries.happened: Amazon indicates near $276, adding to Friday's 15.3% gain with nothing new reported.
figures: Behind it: AWS $42.2B, +37%; backlog $496B; capex guide ~$220B, all from Thursday night
entries.why: A third consecutive session of buying after a 15% gap is the useful signal here. Gaps that keep filling upward on volume mean long-term holders re-rated the business, rather than traders chasing a headline. Cheaper fuel also cuts Amazon's delivery cost and leaves households more to spend, which reaches the retail half directly.

foot.v: Friday's move is settled and largely priced. Today's premarket is not a reaction to anything, since no new figure has been released.
AWS growth slows next quarter while $220B of capex keeps running, turning the spend into a margin problem before the backlog converts.
Q3 results, late October.

entries.happened: Marvell indicates near $184.52 with no company news at all, on a day the wider market is up.
figures: Friday close $187.56, +2.3%, having been up 8.8% intraday
Marvell has not reported this quarter and has announced nothing since June
entries.why: Falling while the index rises is the whole story. Long yields did not fall with oil, and Marvell's custom-silicon programmes are funded years ahead of the revenue they produce. When the cost of that money stays high, investors pay less per dollar of future earnings, whatever crude does.

foot.v: There is nothing company-specific to price. Do not read this as a Marvell event. It is the same funding-cost split that killed Friday's chip rally.
The 30-year yield breaks back below 5%, which would restore the discount rate the group was valued on in June.
Q2 FY27 results, expected late August, not yet company-confirmed.

entries.happened: Intel indicates near $88.80, a second day of giving back Friday's early spike.
figures: Friday: opened $96.72, high $97.90, closed $90.20, -1.0% on the day
Its quarter was 23 July. No filing or announcement since
entries.why: Intel opened Friday up 6% and closed down 1%, and is now lower again. That pattern is capital cost, not chip demand. Intel funds the most expensive build-out on this list and earns the least from it today, so it is the purest read on what expensive long money does to a rebuild story.

foot.v: No news to price. Flag the shape rather than the level: two sessions of selling into strength usually means holders are using rallies to leave.
A named foundry customer signs with a dollar value attached, which would put revenue against the capital for the first time.
Q3 results, late October.

entries.happened: Nebius indicates near $188 with nothing announced since July.
figures: Friday close $190.41, +1.1%, after trading as high as $204.57
Its $1B Reflection AI contract was 14 July. Q2 results are set for 12 August
entries.why: Nebius borrows to build data centres and bills the capacity out later, so it is the most rate-sensitive name here. Falling on a risk-on morning tells you the market is still pricing the cost of that debt, not the contracts. The gap between its $40B-plus contracted revenue and its share price is a financing question.

foot.v: No company news in the window. This is the rates trade reaching the most leveraged name on the list.
The 12 August results show contracted revenue converting to cash faster than the build-out consumes it.
12 August, Q2 results, before the open.

entries.happened: Meta indicates near $563.50, extending Friday's 3.3% gain on no fresh news.
figures: Its capex guide of $130–145B came with the 29 July quarter
entries.why: Meta sits between the two groups: heavy spending, but funded from advertising cash. Lower oil helps twice, by easing the discount rate and by leaving consumers with more to spend, which is what advertisers bid against. That second channel is why it can rise with software rather than with the chipmakers.

foot.v: Premarket only, and no event behind it. Provisional.
Yields resume climbing, which in July made the $130–145B capex look like a cost rather than an investment.
Q3 results, late October.

entries.happened: Tesla indicates near $314 with nothing company-specific since its 2 July delivery figures.
entries.why: Worth one caution. Cheaper petrol is a mild negative for Tesla, because it shrinks the running-cost saving that sells an electric car. The stock is up anyway, which means it is trading with the index this morning rather than on its own economics.

foot.v: July China registrations, due in the coming days.

entries.happened: Apple indicates near $310, steadying after Friday's 7.4% fall.
figures: The $0.27 dividend, declared 30 July, goes ex on 10 August
entries.why: A third of a percent after a 7.4% fall is not a rebound, it is an absence of sellers. The supply-constraint guidance that caused Friday's drop is unchanged, and nothing has been released since. Treat the flat premarket as no new information, not as relief.

foot.v: 10 August, dividend ex-date. Tim Cook hands over to John Ternus on 1 September.

entries.happened: Nvidia indicates near $200, slightly lower, with no company news in the window.
entries.why: Small in size, useful in direction. Nvidia falling while Microsoft rises nearly 2% is the day's split in one pair. The market is paying this morning for AI revenue that already exists and marking down the equipment that has to be financed first.

foot.v: 26 August, Q2 FY27 results.

entries.happened: The IPO roadshow for Robinhood Ventures Fund II opens to the public today at noon ET.
figures: Friday close $86.56, -0.05%; premarket $86.75, about +0.2% on thin trade
RVII filed its Form N-2 on 30 June 2026. No offering size or price has been disclosed
entries.why: This is a dated event with no number attached, so it stays minor until the size is filed. The reason to watch it: a second venture fund would add fee income that recurs, unlike trading revenue that rises and falls with volumes. Investors pay more per dollar of predictable fees.

foot.v: The pricing filing shows a fund large enough to move Robinhood's fee line, rather than a marketing exercise.

readthrough.title: Oil fell 7%. Long yields fell 4 basis points. That gap explains the whole list
readthrough.body: Last week's story was that expensive oil was driving inflation, and inflation was driving the yield that crushed long-duration tech. The weekend removed the oil. The yield stayed. The 30-year sits at 5.226%, four basis points off a 19-year high, after crude gave back a month of gains in one weekend. So the funding problem was never the war. Now watch the same dividing line reappear, premarket, exactly as it did on Friday. The names that fund growth from their own cash flow are up: Microsoft +1.8%, Alphabet +1.8%, Amazon +1.6%, Meta +1.2%. The names that fund it from capital markets are down: Marvell -1.6%, Intel -1.6%, Nebius -1.3%, Nvidia -0.4%. Two AI stories, opposite directions, on a morning when neither had any news. The asymmetry worth holding on to is Microsoft against Nvidia. Both sell the same boom. This morning the market pays for the one that already collects the revenue and discounts the one that must build the capacity first. Tonight's Palantir print is the clean test: it sells enterprise AI software with no capital intensity at all, so a strong US commercial number would confirm buyers are choosing monetisation over machinery, and a weak one would suggest they are simply hiding in size.

note.title: What is not today's news
note.body: Ten of the twelve had nothing company-specific in the window. The weekend produced no earnings, no filings and no contracts for this list, which is normal for a Saturday and Sunday. Everything moving before the bell is the Iran headline and the rates backdrop. Be careful with recycled coverage this morning: Apple's quarter was 30 July, Amazon's and Meta's were 29 July, Microsoft's was 28 July, Intel's was 23 July, Alphabet's and Tesla's were 22 July. Nebius's $1B Reflection AI contract was 14 July. Marvell has not reported. None of that is news from the past 24 hours.
